author: Thomas
authority: Chief Justice Stone-Zsela; he assigns this lead opinion.
form: One signed opinion of the Court: Part I substantive agreement rule, Part II seven-Associate procedural basis for correcting the appellate rule, Part III bounded reversal and remand. Stevens joins Part I and dissents from judgment; Stone joins Parts I and III only. These scope distinctions precede assignment counts.
reason: Thomas's Salinas opinion supplies concrete experience separating agreement to an unlawful undertaking from completion of its acts. His frozen Recio position expressly preserves the different statute's elements, the Government's accepted burden and Rule 30 consequences, so that experience does not import RICO law or dispose of the remaining appellate questions. O'Connor is the strongest pool alternative because Shabani addresses the same statute and a limited remand; Thomas can faithfully apply that settled rule and the agreed procedural distinction with the lower count. The seven full joiners already support the bounded correction. Stone's disposition agreement and joins in Parts I and III do not make him eligible for the additional Part II rationale, and Stevens's substantive agreement does not make him a judgment supporter.
